title: What If You Stood on the Surface of Venus?

scenes.text: What if you landed on Venus? The ground is hot enough to melt lead.
The surface sits around four hundred sixty-five degrees Celsius, hotter than any kitchen oven.
The air presses down with about ninety times Earth's pressure, like sitting nine hundred meters under the sea.
It's almost all carbon dioxide, and the clouds high above are made of sulfuric acid.
In 1982 the Soviet lander Venera 13 survived on the surface for one hundred twenty-seven minutes.
You wouldn't last that long. Venus is the one planet where the ground fights back.
